title: Less Thinking, More Drinking
reading:
"Less thinking, more drinking."

We live in a world that trains us to analyze everything. We want answers, explanations, and understanding. While there's value in thinking, it can become a barrier when it replaces experiencing God.

A scattered mind makes it difficult to recognize a present God. When your thoughts are constantly racing, it becomes harder to rest, to listen, and to adore.

God is not primarily looking for your analysis — He's looking for your attention. He desires adoration more than explanation.

To drink of God means to receive, to sit in His presence, to let your heart be filled without needing to figure everything out. It's a posture of trust.

When you shift from constant mental exploration to simple adoration, you begin to experience Him in ways that thinking alone could never produce.
reflection: What distractions or thought patterns keep your mind from settling in God's presence?
abide: God, quiet the noise within me. Help me to slow down, to be still, and to truly experience Your presence. Teach me to rest my mind and open my heart.
